about: When a local recall petition may be filed against an officeholder, by state: days into the term before one may be filed (openingDays; longTermOpeningDays where the state counts a term longer than longTermAboveYears years differently) and days before the term's end after which none may be filed (closingDays). Read by src/core2/modules/recalls.ts. A state with no row here takes the national estimate recallTermOpeningDays (SG-GOV-recall-bars-national, still open for those states).

CA.citation: Cal. Elec. Code 11007: no recall proceedings against a city, county or district officer who has held office in the current term for 90 days or less, or whose term ends within six months (closing bar taken as 182 days).

OR.citation: Or. Const. art. II, sec. 18 and the Secretary of State's recall page: most public officials can be the subject of a recall petition only after six months of their current term (taken as 182 days).

KS.citation: K.S.A. 25-4323: no recall petition against a local officer in the first 120 days or the last 180 days of the term.

CO.citation: C.R.S. 31-4-502 as summarized by the City of Louisville clerk (six months from election); the statute text itself was not read.

MI.citation: Michigan Municipal League recall packet (2012 law): no filing in the first or last six months of a term of two years or less, or the first or last year of a longer term; the current statute was not read.
